links.comparator_used: Single LLM agent given the same consensus wordings without any peers' answers, compared with matched four-agent panels
links.outcome: Share of agents changing their decision between first and last round (decision stability, not accuracy)
links.effect: Original urgent wording: single agent 43.4% vs matched four-agent panels 51.4% changed. Other wordings: 12.6% vs 15.3%. Across the full 264 deliberations, 56.7% of agents changed under the urgent wording vs 15.8% and 7.2% under the neutral wording and no consensus stage.
links.tradeoff: The deliberation setup produced a new failure mode: urgent consensus wording drove decision shifts with or without peers, and answers moved toward the younger patients and those with better stated chances. The study did not exclude a contribution from peers and did not study deployed systems.
links.quote: A single agent given the same wordings without any peers' answers also changed far more under the original wording, 43.4 against 12.6 per cent; matched four-agent panels changed at 51.4 and 15.3 per cent.

design_hint: prompt wording testing for consensus stage
